content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Compare the physical properties of metals and non-metals
Compare the chemical properties of metals and non-metals
Locate metals, non-metals, and metalloids in the periodic table
Explain the differences in terms of structure and bonding
Elements can be broadly classified as
based on their properties. About 80% of elements are metals, but non-metals include many important elements like carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen.

Silicon is a metalloid. Explain what this means and why it is useful.
A metalloid has properties between metals and non-metals
Silicon has a shiny appearance (like metals)
It conducts electricity, but not as well as metals
Its conductivity increases when heated or doped with impurities
This property is essential for computer chips
Silicon is the basis of the electronics industry
Thinking hydrogen is a metal because it's on the left
Hydrogen is a non-metal (gas, doesn't conduct)
Non-metals can be solids (C, S, I₂), liquids (Br₂), or gases
Graphite is an exception - it has delocalised electrons
